## 任务：检查 westd-19828 两张 GPU 利用率

### 背景
19828 上有 2 个 1.4B 实验：
- cuda:0: scale_14b_t15_a075_s42_fp32 (PID 793171)
- cuda:1: scale_14b_t10_a050_s42_fp32_v2 (PID 776064)

需要确认两个进程正常运行，GPU 利用率是否正常。

### 步骤（全部用 ssh_read_only）

1. GPU 状态：
```bash
nvidia-smi
```

2. 详细 GPU 利用率（多次采样，看是否波动）：
```bash
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used,memory.total,temperature.gpu --format=csv,noheader
```

3. 确认进程存活：
```bash
ps -p 793171 -o pid,pcpu,pmem,rss,etime,args 2>/dev/null || echo "PID 793171 DEAD"
ps -p 776064 -o pid,pcpu,pmem,rss,etime,args 2>/dev/null || echo "PID 776064 DEAD"
```

4. 如果 GPU 利用率 < 80%，检查 IO bound：
```bash
iostat -x 1 3 2>/dev/null | tail -20 || echo "NO_IOSTAT"
top -bn1 | head -20
df -h /root/autodl-tmp/
```

5. 检查训练日志最后几行确认进展：
```bash
tail -5 /root/autodl-tmp/distrib_canary_collapse/outputs/scale_14b_t15_a075_s42_fp32/*.log 2>/dev/null
tail -5 /root/autodl-tmp/distrib_canary_collapse/results/phase_diagram/t10_a050_s42_fp32_14b/*.log 2>/dev/null
```
如果找不到 log，用 find 搜索：
```bash
find /root/autodl-tmp/distrib_canary_collapse -name "*.log" -newer /root/autodl-tmp/distrib_canary_collapse/outputs -type f 2>/dev/null | head -10
```

6. 检查当前 generation 进度：
```bash
ls -d /root/autodl-tmp/distrib_canary_collapse/outputs/scale_14b_t15_a075_s42_fp32/gen_* 2>/dev/null | sort -V
ls -d /root/autodl-tmp/distrib_canary_collapse/results/phase_diagram/t10_a050_s42_fp32_14b/gen_* 2>/dev/null | sort -V
```

### 汇报
- 两张卡 GPU 利用率
- 两个进程是否存活
- 当前 generation 进度
- 如果利用率低，分析原因（IO bound / CPU bound / 其他）

# FPR Sensitivity Analysis: PermG at 10% FPR

We evaluate the robustness of the MMCT consensus framework under the conservative assumption that PermG's true FPR could be as high as 10% (the upper bound of a cluster-adjusted confidence interval with only 3 seed-clusters). Even under this assumption, PermG remains the lowest-FPR method among the five in our framework: the next-best method (Toda-Yamamoto) has a pooled FPR of 16.7%, followed by Threshold Onset at 25.0%, Differenced Cross-Correlation at 37.5%, and Naive Cross-Correlation at 91.7%. Crucially, our primary results rely on equal-weight K≥3 majority voting, where each method contributes exactly one vote regardless of its FPR—this mechanism is completely unaffected by any FPR assumption. For the exploratory FPR-inverse weighting analysis, PermG's weight drops from effectively infinite (at observed 0%) to 10.0 (at hypothetical 10%), but this still exceeds all alternatives (TY: 6.0, Threshold: 4.0, DiffXCorr: 2.67), preserving the full rank ordering. The insensitivity of both the voting mechanism and the method ranking to this worst-case FPR assumption provides strong evidence that the MMCT framework's conclusions are robust to uncertainty in PermG's Type I error rate.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}

We study lead-lag analysis design considerations in iterative training collapse using Pythia-410M~\cite{biderman2023pythia} (410M parameters, decoder-only), with cross-architecture validation on GPT-2-medium (345M) and three additional families (\S\ref{sec:generalization}).
Training data is drawn from WikiText-103~\cite{merity2017pointer} following the replace paradigm of~\citet{shumailov2024curse}: each generation fine-tunes on a mixture of $\alpha$ synthetic and $(1{-}\alpha)$ real data, generates 5{,}000 replacement samples, and fully replaces the synthetic pool (hyperparameters in Appendix~\ref{app:training_details}).
We run $T{=}10$ generations across 13 contamination levels ($\alpha \in \{0.00, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.40, 0.45, 0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.75, 1.00\}$, including null control) with multi-seed replication (4 seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$; 3 at primary levels).

We track two \emph{canary metrics}---token entropy and ECE---and three \emph{downstream metrics}: distinct-1, distinct-2~\cite{li2016diversity}, and perplexity.
All hypothesis tests apply BH-FDR correction at $q{=}0.05$; PermG uses 5{,}000 permutations on first-differenced series~\cite{shojaie2022granger} with maximum lag~5.


\subsection{Sharp Detection Onset}
\label{sec:regime}

Diversity collapse occurs at every contamination level: distinct-1 declines by $14.1\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$ (fine-tuning drift) and by $40.3{\pm}0.3\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.25$ (3-seed mean).
Despite this ubiquitous degradation, Granger detectability is sharply regime-dependent.
The onset we report reflects PermG's statistical power curve crossing the detection threshold at a critical contamination level, not the emergence of a new physical signal; this interpretation is confirmed by sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
Permutation Granger (PermG) tests find 0/8 canary$\to$downstream pairs FDR-significant from $\alpha{=}0.00$ through $\alpha{=}0.45$, then jump to 6/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ (2~fp32 seeds, consistent).
This transition is striking because cumulative synthetic fraction barely changes across the boundary: $C = 1{-}(1{-}\alpha)^{10}$ yields $99.75\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.45$ versus $99.90\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.50$, a difference of 0.15 percentage points, yet detection jumps from null to reliable.
Sigmoid regression on the 13-point $T{=}10$ grid yields $\alpha_c = 0.483 \pm 0.006$ ($R^2 = 0.969$); dense $\alpha$ sampling (17~values) constrains the onset steepness to $k{=}15.7$ (95\% CI $[9.4, 28.2]$), a steep but finite-width sigmoid (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}).
This single-$T$ estimate is consistent with the cross-$T$ validated model (\S\ref{sec:theory}), which predicts how the detection boundary shifts with observation length ($\gamma{=}2.08$).
The transition is not a literal step function ($\Delta\mathrm{AIC}{=}-110$ favoring sigmoid; Appendix~\ref{app:sigmoid_shape}), but its steepness (${\approx}3{\times}$ smooth-model predictions; \S\ref{sec:theory}) exceeds what PermG power curves alone produce.
At $T{=}10$, PermG power is ${\approx}37\%$ (Appendix~\ref{app:power_sim}), partly amplifying the $0/8{\to}6/8$ sharpness; however, onset steepness ($k{=}15.7$, ${\approx}3{\times}$ smooth predictions) and cross-seed consistency ($0/8{\to}6/8$ at $\alpha{=}0.48{\to}0.50$ in both seeds) argue for a genuine, power-modulated transition.
A Fisher exact test corroborates the categorical jump: 0/64 pairs FDR-significant at $\alpha \leq 0.45$ versus 18/32 at $\alpha \geq 0.50$ ($p = 3.45 \times 10^{-11}$); sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ ($p_{\mathrm{fdr}} = 0.059$--$0.091$) are consistent with proximity to the power boundary (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
A systematic robustness analysis (1{,}160 configurations) confirms specification-invariance of the onset.

First-differencing scopes the canary claim precisely.
Canary$\to$diversity pairs retain unanimous FDR significance after first-differencing ($24/24 \to 24/24$ across 4~seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$, 6 pairs per seed), while canary$\to$perplexity collapses entirely ($F \approx 0$, $p = 0.99$): the apparent perplexity association is a shared-trend artifact.
All canary claims are therefore scoped to diversity metrics only.
This scoping reflects a genuine temporal structure difference, not selective power loss from differencing: $|r|$ retention is ${\geq}95\%$ for both channels, but canary$\to$diversity correlations peak at lagged offsets (81\% at lag${<}0$, median${=}-1$) while canary$\to$perplexity correlations are contemporaneous (50\% at lag${=}0$), producing $20$--$28{\times}$ lower Granger $F$ for perplexity (Appendix~\ref{app:channel_effect_size}; perplexity $n{=}8$, limited sample).
At $\alpha{=}1.0$, all 24 canary$\to$diversity pairs (6 per seed $\times$ 4~seeds; mauve excluded) reach FDR significance in the forward direction with 0/24 reverse; directional asymmetry is robust across all WikiText conditions.
Independent of the Granger test, the degradation cascade confirms temporal precedence: entropy onset at generation~1 precedes distinct-$n$ onset at generation~2 in 16/18 WikiText conditions (Kendall $\tau{=}0.337$; \S\ref{sec:cascade}, Appendix~\ref{app:moment_cascade}).
The canary mechanism also exhibits a blind spot: at $\alpha{=}0.10$, distinct-1 has already dropped by $39.6\%$, yet token entropy is indistinguishable from the null ($-5.3\%$ versus $-4.6{\pm}0.4\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$).
The gen-1 entropy deviation spans three orders of magnitude across the $\alpha$ range: $0.5\sigma$ at $\alpha{=}0.10$ to $60\sigma$ at $\alpha{=}0.75$ (relative to null variability), explaining why the blind zone persists despite increasing contamination.\footnote{Seed~43 at $\alpha{=}0.10$ shows 3/8 versus 0/8 for seed~42; no other sub-threshold level exhibits seed-dependent detection.}
Below $\alpha_c$ at $T{=}10$, diversity collapse proceeds without any detectable Granger-precedence signal in the canary metrics.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.9\textwidth]{figures/metric_trajectory.pdf}
\caption{Metric trajectories at $\alpha{=}1.0$ (Pythia-410M, 4~seeds). Token entropy drops at generation~1; distinct-1 declines from generations~2--3, with a consistent one-generation canary lead across all four seeds (shaded: inter-seed range). This pattern corresponds to 24/24 forward and 0/24 reverse FDR-significant canary$\to$diversity pairs (6 per seed, mauve excluded).}
\label{fig:metric_trajectory}
\end{figure*}


\subsection{Dose-Response and Detection Regimes}
\label{sec:dose_response}

The PermG dose-response profile (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}) reveals four detection regimes: \emph{blind} ($\alpha \leq 0.45$, 0/8 FDR-significant pairs), \emph{onset} ($\alpha \approx 0.50$, 6/8), \emph{non-monotonic dip} ($\alpha \approx 0.60$, 0/8), and \emph{detection} ($\alpha{\geq}0.75$, 6/8 across 4~seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$).
At $\alpha{=}0.60$, PermG returns $0/8$ at $T{\leq}20$ but recovers to $5/8$ at $T{=}25$, confirming a transient dip that $\sqrt{T}$ power eventually overcomes (Appendix~\ref{app:t20_comparison}).

Method choice is itself a major source of variability: at $\alpha{=}1.0$, direction-checked forward significance spans 0\% to 75\% (Table~\ref{tab:method_comparison}), with $\kappa{=}0.185$; a specification curve (18~variants; Appendix~\ref{app:spec_curve}) confirms onset invariance.
Task degradation corroborates: perplexity jumps $+31\%$ between $\alpha{=}0.50$ and $0.52$ (Appendix~\ref{app:task_degradation}).


\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Forward-direction FDR significance rates (\%) across contamination levels (Pythia-410M, seed~42, fp32; $3\sigma$ threshold calibration, lag-direction filtering for cross-correlation methods). Each cell: fraction of 8 validated pairs at BH-corrected significance ($q{=}0.05$). PermG is the only method combining zero null-control FPR with consistent detection at $\alpha \geq 0.50$.}
\label{tab:method_comparison}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{lcccccc}
\toprule
Method & $\alpha{=}0.0$ & $\alpha{=}0.25$ & $\alpha{=}0.50$ & $\alpha{=}0.75$ & $\alpha{=}1.0$ & FPR$_\text{null}$ \\
\midrule
Naive XCorr          & 75   & 62.5 & 62.5 & 0    & 0    & 75  \\
Diff.\ XCorr         & 0    & 25   & 12.5 & 0    & 0    & 0   \\
Threshold ($3\sigma$) & 37.5 & 62.5 & 100  & 100  & 25   & 37.5 \\
Perm.\ Granger       & \textbf{0}    & \textbf{0}    & \textbf{75}   & \textbf{75}   & \textbf{75}   & \textbf{0}   \\
Toda--Yamamoto$^\S$  & 12.5 & 37.5 & 50   & 100  & 12.5 & 12.5 \\
\bottomrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\footnotesize $^\S$TY directional assignment under verification; row retained for completeness.} \\
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\footnotesize Pooled FPR (3 seeds, cluster-bootstrap 95\% CI): \S\ref{sec:mmct}.} \\
\end{tabular}}
\end{table}


\subsection{Detection Boundary Left-Shift}
\label{sec:t20}

The detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ decreases monotonically: $\alpha_c(5){\geq}1.0$, $\alpha_c(10){=}0.487$, consistent with $T^{-2.08}$ power scaling (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
The $\alpha{=}0.45$ column traces the sharpest validation: $0/8$ at $T{\leq}10$, $6/8$ at $T{=}15$ (dual-seed), $5/8$ at $T{=}20$, $6/8$ at $T{=}25$.
The systematic 2/8 gap reflects MAUVE floor saturation ($\mu{=}0.029$, SNR $4.68$ vs diversity $6.40$--$8.20$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
Cross-seed replication shows PermG within ${\pm}1$, though boundary cells exhibit sensitivity: $[0, 6]/8$ at ($T{=}10$, $\alpha{=}0.50$); $[0, 3]/8$ at ($T{=}20$, $\alpha{=}0.60$).
Minimum $T$ for 80\% power at $\alpha{=}0.50$ is approximately $T{=}30$ (extrapolated from simulation; Appendix~\ref{app:power_sim}).
The $\alpha{=}0.60$ dip dissolves by $T{=}25$ ($5/8$), validating $\sqrt{T}$ power scaling; predict-then-verify (commit \texttt{bad72cc}) yields 2/4 boundary predictions within CI (Appendix~\ref{app:t20_prediction_timeline}).


\subsection{Cross-Architecture Validation}
\label{sec:generalization}

We evaluate PermG across 15 model-seed combinations spanning five families, scales 345M--6.9B, and two domains (Table~\ref{tab:generalization}).
PermG reaches ${\geq}6/8$ in 10/15 conditions where entropy declines monotonically before diversity; C4 yields strongest detection (Pythia-1.4B: 2/8 WikiText $\to$ 8/8 C4).
The 5 non-confirming conditions span four failure modes: precision sensitivity (GPT-2 bf16: 0/8 vs fp32: 6/8), bidirectional confounding (GPT-2 s43), seed dependence (Pythia-1.4B: s42 2/8, s43 6/8), and architecture-specific decoupling (SmolLM3-3B: 3/8, entropy 0/4).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Cross-architecture PermG forward detection ($\alpha{=}1.0$, 15 model-seed combinations across five families and two domains).}
\label{tab:generalization}
\begin{tabular}{lrcl}
\toprule
Model & Params & Domain & PermG fwd \\
\midrule
Pythia-410M    & 410M & Wiki & \textbf{6/8} \\
Pythia-1.4B    & 1.4B & Wiki & 2--6/8$^\dagger$ \\
Pythia-6.9B    & 6.9B & Wiki & \textbf{7/8}$^*$ \\
GPT-2-medium   & 345M & Wiki & \textbf{6/8}$^\S$ \\
OPT-1.3B       & 1.3B & Wiki & \textbf{6/8} \\
Qwen3.5-0.8B   & 0.8B & Wiki & \textbf{8/8} \\
SmolLM3-3B     & 3.0B & Wiki & 3/8$^\ddagger$ \\
Padding-410M   & 410M & Wiki & \textbf{6/8} \\
\addlinespace
Pythia-1B      & 1.0B & C4   & \textbf{8/8} \\
Pythia-1.4B    & 1.4B & C4   & \textbf{8/8} \\
\bottomrule
\multicolumn{4}{l}{\footnotesize $^\dagger$Seed-dep.\ (s42: 2/8, s43: 6/8). $^*$bf16. $^\ddagger$ECE-only (ent.\ 0/4).} \\
\multicolumn{4}{l}{\footnotesize $^\S$s42 fp32: 6/8 fwd, 0 rev; s43: 6/8 both; bf16: 0/8.} \\
\multicolumn{4}{l}{\footnotesize 2 seeds each for Pythia-410M/1.4B, GPT-2, OPT, Pythia-1B C4.} \\
\end{tabular}
\end{table}


\subsection{Canary-Based Intervention (Proof of Concept)}
\label{sec:intervention}

As an illustrative proof-of-concept under favorable conditions ($\alpha{=}1.0$, full replacement), we implement predictive cessation: training switches to pure real data when token entropy drops ${>}15\%$ from generation~0.
The 15\% threshold was selected post-hoc on training data without held-out validation; it lies within a robust operating band $[10\%, 22\%]$ where all thresholds produce zero false alarms at $\alpha{=}0.0$ (Appendix~\ref{app:intervention_sensitivity}).
A reactive baseline triggers on distinct-1 drop ${>}10\%$.
The predictive trigger fires at generation~1 (one generation before reactive) in both Pythia-410M and Pythia-1.4B, reducing peak perplexity by 58\% ($56.99$ vs.\ $157.09$; bootstrap 95\% CI: 29--64\%).
This single-setting demonstration is not rigorously evaluated: threshold selection, $\alpha{<}1.0$ performance, and multi-domain generalization remain open.

1	\subsection{Sharp Detection Onset}
2	\label{sec:regime}
3	
4	Diversity collapse occurs at every contamination level: distinct-1 declines by $14.1\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$ (fine-tuning drift) and by $40.3{\pm}0.3\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.25$ (3-seed mean).
5	Despite this ubiquitous degradation, Granger-causal detectability is sharply regime-dependent.
6	Permutation Granger (PermG) tests find 0/8 canary$\to$downstream pairs FDR-significant from $\alpha{=}0.00$ through $\alpha{=}0.45$, then jump to 6/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ (2~fp32 seeds, consistent).
7	This transition is striking because cumulative synthetic fraction barely changes across the boundary: $C = 1{-}(1{-}\alpha)^{10}$ yields $99.75\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.45$ versus $99.90\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.50$, a difference of 0.15 percentage points, yet detection jumps from null to reliable.
8	Sigmoid regression across the 13-point $\alpha$ grid quantifies this steep onset: $\alpha_c = 0.476$ at $T{=}10$, steepness $k \geq 200$, transition width $\Delta\alpha \approx 0.02$, $R^2 = 0.969$ (versus power-law $R^2 = 0.808$, $\Delta\mathrm{AIC} = 18.2$; Figure~\ref{fig:phase_transition}).
9	At $\alpha{=}0.45$, PermG $p$-values reveal sub-threshold signal ($p_{\mathrm{fdr}} = 0.059$ for seed~43, $0.091$ for seed~42), consistent with the power-threshold interpretation of $\alpha_c$ at $T{=}10$ (\S\ref{sec:theory}): the onset reflects PermG's power curve crossing the detection floor, not the emergence of a new physical signal.
10	A specification curve analysis spanning 1{,}160 analytical specifications confirms that the sharp detection onset is specification-invariant.
11	
12	First-differencing scopes the canary claim precisely.
13	Canary$\to$diversity pairs retain unanimous FDR significance after first-differencing ($24/24 \to 24/24$ across 4~seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$), while canary$\to$perplexity collapses entirely ($F \approx 0$, $p = 0.99$): the apparent perplexity association is a shared-trend artifact.
14	All canary claims are therefore scoped to diversity metrics only.
15	At $\alpha{=}1.0$, 24/24 forward-direction pairs reach FDR significance with 0/24 reverse (4~seeds); directional asymmetry is robust across all WikiText conditions.
16	The canary mechanism also exhibits a blind spot: at $\alpha{=}0.10$, distinct-1 has already dropped by $39.6\%$, yet token entropy is indistinguishable from the null ($-5.3\%$ versus $-4.6{\pm}0.4\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$).\footnote{Seed~43 at $\alpha{=}0.10$ shows 3/8 PermG FDR-significant pairs versus 0/8 for seed~42, consistent with stochastic variation at low signal rather than robust detection; no other below-threshold $\alpha$ level exhibits seed-dependent detection.}
17	Below $\alpha_c$ at $T{=}10$, diversity collapse proceeds without any detectable Granger-causal signal in the canary metrics.
18

22	\caption{Metric trajectories at $\alpha{=}1.0$ (Pythia-410M, 4~seeds). Token entropy drops at generation~1; distinct-1 declines from generations~2--3, with a consistent one-generation canary lead across all four seeds (shaded: inter-seed range). This pattern corresponds to 24/24 forward and 0/24 reverse FDR-significant pairs.}
23	\label{fig:metric_trajectory}
24	\end{figure}
25	
26	
27	\subsection{Dose-Response and the $S \times R$ Framework}
28	\label{sec:dose_response}
29	
30	The PermG dose-response profile (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}) reveals four detection regimes: \emph{blind} ($\alpha \leq 0.45$, 0/8 FDR-significant pairs), \emph{onset} ($\alpha \approx 0.50$, 6/8), \emph{synchronous dip} ($\alpha \approx 0.60$, 0/8 both seeds; dual-seed confirmed), and \emph{detection} ($\alpha{=}0.75$, 0--6/8 per seed, 2 of 3 seeds ${\geq}5/8$; $\alpha{=}1.0$, 6/8 across 4~seeds).
31	The non-monotonic dip at $\alpha{=}0.60$ is consistent with the $S \times R$ framework (\S\ref{sec:theory}): signal strength $S(\alpha)$ rises monotonically with contamination, but temporal resolution $R(\alpha)$ drops when relaxation time approaches the observation interval.
32	At $\alpha \approx 0.60$, this compression drives the canary-to-downstream lag toward zero, and the product $S \times R$ reaches a local minimum.
33	The synchronous zone is mechanistically distinct from the blind spot: in the blind zone, canary drift is indistinguishable from the null; in the synchronous zone, both canary and downstream metrics drift substantially but without temporal offset.
34	At $\alpha{=}0.55$, PermG returns 0/8 FDR-significant pairs despite marginal $p$-values ($p_{\mathrm{fdr}}{=}0.062$--$0.092$), consistent with power-limited non-detection between onset and synchronous dip; differenced cross-correlation detects 8/8 bidirectionally at this level, confirming that a lead-lag signal exists but falls below PermG's directional detection threshold.

\subsection{Sharp Detection Onset}
\label{sec:regime}

Diversity collapse occurs at every contamination level: distinct-1 declines by $14.1\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$ (fine-tuning drift) and by $40.3{\pm}0.3\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.25$ (3-seed mean).
Despite this ubiquitous degradation, Granger-causal detectability is sharply regime-dependent.
Permutation Granger (PermG) tests find 0/8 canary$\to$downstream pairs FDR-significant from $\alpha{=}0.00$ through $\alpha{=}0.45$, then jump to 6/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ (2~fp32 seeds, consistent).
This transition is striking because cumulative synthetic fraction barely changes across the boundary: $C = 1{-}(1{-}\alpha)^{10}$ yields $99.75\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.45$ versus $99.90\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.50$, a difference of 0.15 percentage points, yet detection jumps from null to reliable.
Sigmoid regression across the 13-point $\alpha$ grid quantifies this steep onset: $\alpha_c = 0.476$ at $T{=}10$, steepness $k \geq 200$, transition width $\Delta\alpha \approx 0.02$, $R^2 = 0.969$ (versus power-law $R^2 = 0.808$, $\Delta\mathrm{AIC} = 18.2$; Figure~\ref{fig:phase_transition}).
At $\alpha{=}0.45$, PermG $p$-values reveal sub-threshold signal ($p_{\mathrm{fdr}} = 0.059$ for seed~43, $0.091$ for seed~42), consistent with the power-threshold interpretation of $\alpha_c$ at $T{=}10$ (\S\ref{sec:theory}): the onset reflects PermG's power curve crossing the detection floor, not the emergence of a new physical signal.
A specification curve analysis spanning 1{,}160 analytical specifications confirms that the sharp detection onset is specification-invariant.

First-differencing scopes the canary claim precisely.
Canary$\to$diversity pairs retain unanimous FDR significance after first-differencing ($24/24 \to 24/24$ across 4~seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$), while canary$\to$perplexity collapses entirely ($F \approx 0$, $p = 0.99$): the apparent perplexity association is a shared-trend artifact.
All canary claims are therefore scoped to diversity metrics only.
At $\alpha{=}1.0$, 24/24 forward-direction pairs reach FDR significance with 0/24 reverse (4~seeds); directional asymmetry is robust across all WikiText conditions.
The canary mechanism also exhibits a blind spot: at $\alpha{=}0.10$, distinct-1 has already dropped by $39.6\%$, yet token entropy is indistinguishable from the null ($-5.3\%$ versus $-4.6{\pm}0.4\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$).\footnote{Seed~43 at $\alpha{=}0.10$ shows 3/8 PermG FDR-significant pairs versus 0/8 for seed~42, consistent with stochastic variation at low signal rather than robust detection; no other below-threshold $\alpha$ level exhibits seed-dependent detection.}
Below $\alpha_c$ at $T{=}10$, diversity collapse proceeds without any detectable Granger-causal signal in the canary metrics.

\caption{Metric trajectories at $\alpha{=}1.0$ (Pythia-410M, 4~seeds). Token entropy drops at generation~1; distinct-1 declines from generations~2--3, with a consistent one-generation canary lead across all four seeds (shaded: inter-seed range). This pattern corresponds to 24/24 forward and 0/24 reverse FDR-significant pairs.}
\label{fig:metric_trajectory}
\end{figure}


\subsection{Dose-Response and the $S \times R$ Framework}
\label{sec:dose_response}

The PermG dose-response profile (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}) reveals four detection regimes: \emph{blind} ($\alpha \leq 0.45$, 0/8 FDR-significant pairs), \emph{onset} ($\alpha \approx 0.50$, 6/8), \emph{synchronous dip} ($\alpha \approx 0.60$, 0/8 both seeds; dual-seed confirmed), and \emph{detection} ($\alpha{=}0.75$, 0--6/8 per seed, 2 of 3 seeds ${\geq}5/8$; $\alpha{=}1.0$, 6/8 across 4~seeds).
The non-monotonic dip at $\alpha{=}0.60$ is consistent with the $S \times R$ framework (\S\ref{sec:theory}): signal strength $S(\alpha)$ rises monotonically with contamination, but temporal resolution $R(\alpha)$ drops when relaxation time approaches the observation interval.
At $\alpha \approx 0.60$, this compression drives the canary-to-downstream lag toward zero, and the product $S \times R$ reaches a local minimum.
The synchronous zone is mechanistically distinct from the blind spot: in the blind zone, canary drift is indistinguishable from the null; in the synchronous zone, both canary and downstream metrics drift substantially but without temporal offset.
At $\alpha{=}0.55$, PermG returns 0/8 FDR-significant pairs despite marginal $p$-values ($p_{\mathrm{fdr}}{=}0.062$--$0.092$), consistent with power-limited non-detection between onset and synchronous dip; differenced cross-correlation detects 8/8 bidirectionally at this level, confirming that a lead-lag signal exists but falls below PermG's directional detection threshold.

Method choice is itself a major source of analytic variability.
At $\alpha{=}1.0$, forward-direction significance rates range from 100\% (naive cross-correlation) to 37.5\% (PermG), with inter-method $\kappa = 0.185$ (near chance) and a spurious rate of at least 62.5\%.
PermG is the only method that combines zero null-control FPR with consistent detection at $\alpha \geq 0.50$ (Table~\ref{tab:method_comparison}); its nonparametric null distribution, built-in directionality, and hyperparameter-free design explain this advantage.
The $S \times R$ framework generates three testable predictions for $T{=}20$ via $\mathrm{Power}(\alpha, T) = \Phi(S \cdot R \cdot \sqrt{T}/\sigma)$: (i)~$\alpha_c$ at $T{=}10$ should left-shift, (ii)~the transition should smooth, and (iii)~different methods should exhibit different $\alpha_c$ values.
These predictions are under empirical verification.

\label{sec:generalization}

We evaluate the sharp detection onset across 15 model-seed combinations spanning six families (Pythia, GPT-2, OPT, Qwen, SmolLM3, Padding-variant), scales from 345M to 6.9B parameters, and two training domains (WikiText-103, C4).

SmolLM3's token entropy exhibits non-monotonic oscillations across generations; this pattern violates the monotonic decline that Granger tests require.
The onset boundary $\alpha_c \approx 0.50$ at $T{=}10$ is architecture-independent: every family that achieves detection does so at or above this threshold, and none achieves reliable detection below it.

At Pythia-6.9B (bf16), detection recovers to 7/8 on WikiText.
Dataset characteristics modulate detection power independently of model capacity.
Directional asymmetry also varies by domain: at $\alpha{=}0.50$ on C4, PermG reverse reaches 7/8, compared to 0/24 across all WikiText conditions.

2	\label{sec:cascade}
3	
4	We formalize the empirical regularity that entropy is the earliest available canary metric for diversity collapse.
5	Under mode amplification---the assumption that MLE on peaked distributions concentrates probability toward high-frequency tokens~\cite{shumailov2024curse,dohmatob2024tale}---we derive a formal ordering of metric responses with theoretical grounding (proofs in Appendix~\ref{app:cascade_theory}).
6	
7	\begin{proposition}[Entropy responds before diversity]\label{thm:entropy_leads}
8	Under mode amplification: \textup{(a)} entropy can decrease while the $\epsilon$-effective support $S_\epsilon(p) {=} |\{i: p_i > \epsilon\}|$ (hence distinct-$n$) is unchanged; \textup{(b)} if distinct-$n$ decreases, entropy has already decreased.
9	\end{proposition}
10	
11	The asymmetry arises because entropy responds to any mass redistribution (first-order), while diversity changes only when a token probability crosses the generation threshold~$\epsilon$; the margin $\gamma = \min_{i: p_i > \epsilon}(p_i - \epsilon)$ quantifies how much shift diversity absorbs silently.
12	
13	\begin{proposition}[Diversity lag $\geq 1$ generation]\label{prop:div_lag}
14	If the per-generation perturbation satisfies $\alpha\|\mathcal{T}(p_t) - p_t\|_\infty < \gamma(p_t, \epsilon)$ through entropy onset $t_H$, then diversity onset $t_D \geq t_H + 1$.
15	\end{proposition}
16	
17	ECE co-moves with entropy at zero lag: peakier conditionals simultaneously decrease per-token entropy and increase confidence ($\Delta\mathrm{ECE} \approx \Delta C > 0$ whenever $\Delta\bar{H} < 0$; qualitative argument, Appendix~\ref{app:cascade_theory}).
